# Colophon {.unnumbered}

Tools change. Platforms disappear. Plain text endures.

*The Book of AI* is authored, versioned, and compiled entirely with open-source/Free-Software, local-first software. No proprietary publishing platforms, no locked databases, and no cloud dependencies are required to read, edit, or rebuild it.

## What colophone is
> Traditionally placed at the very end of a physical book, a colophon is a brief note describing how the book was manufactured—the paper, ink, typeface, and printing press. In a modern technical book, it documents the software toolchain: plain-text Markdown (.qmd), Quarto, Pandoc, Git, your linter configuration, and the fonts or theme used.

## The Press

| Layer        | Tool                       | Role                                                     |
|--------------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| **Source**   | Quarto (`.qmd`) & Markdown | Plain-text authoring and modular lab includes            |
| **Compiler** | Quarto CLI & Pandoc        | Renders HTML, PDF, and EPUB from one source tree         |
| **Quality**  | `markdownlint-cli2`        | Enforces formatting via `.markdownlint.jsonc`            |
| **Archive**  | Git & GitHub               | Version history, issue tracking, and public distribution |

## Building an Offline Copy

Anyone can clone the repository and run the press locally—no internet connection required after the initial clone:

```bash
git clone [https://github.com/DavidGeeraerts/AI.git](https://github.com/DavidGeeraerts/AI.git)
cd AI
quarto render
